name: geometry-percent-viewport-strap
exporter: Sketch 100 (sketchtool export), then hand-edited into a "responsive SVG" for a web page
story: A sponsor strap that already lived on a department web page, where someone replaced its pixel width and height with 100% and added a preserveAspectRatio so it would scale in the layout.
idioms: width="100%" height="100%" - a percentage where every other file in the corpus has a number, so the only real size left in the document is the viewBox
an explicit preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet", which is the default value written out by hand rather than omitted

the Sketch shell underneath: <title> and <desc>Created with Sketch.</desc> as the first two children, the fixed reset group <g stroke="none" stroke-width="1" fill="none" fill-rule="evenodd">, layer names dasherised into ids (id="Sponsor-strap", id="Strap-plate")
explicit closing tags on empty elements (<rect ...></rect>) rather than self-closing
text as <text id=..><tspan x=.. y=..>…</tspan></text> with the baseline on the tspan and the typography on the parent
font-family="Archivo-Bold, Archivo" - PostScript face first, family second - with font-weight repeated alongside
unitless letter-spacing="4" as a presentation attribute, 4-space indentation
whyThisMatters: Rule 1 says a viewBox OR width+height gives the file its size, and every fixture so far has had both agree or had only one of them. This is the file where width and height are present, parse as a number, and mean nothing - 100% of a viewport that does not exist yet. A size reader that reaches for width/height too eagerly lands on a 100 x 100 design space and puts every field position off by a factor of nineteen, while reporting a plausible-looking number rather than failing. It is also the direct guard on the unit conversion the millimetre and point files ask for: the fix must convert mm and pt and must NOT be tempted by a percentage. Taking a graphic off a web page is a normal way to acquire one.
